messages.subject_clean: Animals that died or were removed
messages.body_plain:
Dear oSCR users;
I used code below to make the scrFrame.
My question is how can I add the indCovs to this scrFrame? For example, all the animals is now 'removed' on last occasion, but I want to specify which day they were removed.
At moment I have the removed data in a DF, structured as Session, AnimalID, TrapID, Occ, Sex, Removed.
Any help will be greatly appreciated.
Thanks
Lourens

sf.liv <- data2oscr(edf = Liv.scr,
                  sess.col = 1,
                  id.col = 2,
                  occ.col = 4,
                  trap.col = 3,
                  tdf = list( SiteA.2017.liv, SiteB.2017.liv, SiteC.2017.liv, SiteD.2017.liv, SiteE.2017.liv),
                  K = c(5,5,5,5,5),
                  ntraps = rep(49,5))$scrFrame

messages.body_plain:
Hi Lourens,

The ‘removed’ has not been integrated into data2oSCR yet – thanks for spotting that. In the meantime, can you try this (make sure the removed lines up correctly with individuals). I’m at  workshop and will fix data2oscr at the end of the week:

sf.liv <- data2oscr(edf = Liv.scr,
                    sess.col = 1,
                    id.col = 2,
                    occ.col = 4,
                    trap.col = 3,

                    tdf = list(SiteA.2017.liv, SiteB.2017.liv,

                               SiteC.2017.liv, SiteD.2017.liv,

                               SiteE.2017.liv),
                    K = c(5,5,5,5,5),
                    ntraps = rep(49,5))$scrFrame

for(i in 1:5){

tmp <- Liv.scr[Liv.scr$Session == i,]

tmp$AnimalID <- factor(tmp$AnimalID)

rmv <- tapply(tmp$AnimalID,tmp$Removed,mean)

sf.liv$indCovs[[i]]$removed <- rmv

}

messages.subject: Projection of latitude and longitude to XY cartesian system
messages.subject_clean: Projection of latitude and longitude to XY cartesian system
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Good morning. I'm working on a set of traps. I have the latitude and longitude where each trap is located. But I understand that I must transform and project latitude and longitude to a system of Cartesian XY coordinates on a scale of meters or kms. I have latitude and longitude in two columns for each trap.

What package R do you recommend to me to do the transformation (projection).

I understand that I cannot use oSCR latitude and longitude directly to define the location of the traps.

Please, correct me if I'm wrong.

Greetings,

Victor

messages.subject: Re: Projection of latitude and longitude to XY cartesian system
messages.subject_clean: Projection of latitude and longitude to XY cartesian system
messages.body_plain:
Hi Victor, this is a general problem that goes far beyond oSCR.  You cannot measure Euclidean distance with latitude and longitude.

Depending on where the study was located, you could choose one of the 60 longitudinal UTM zones on which to project the coordinates.  The following link provides some guidance in R:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/18639967/converting-latitude-and-longitude-points-to-utm

And here is a map of the longitudinal zones to choose.  I believe R should be able to handle the appropriate latitudinal zone.
http://www.dmap.co.uk/utmworld.htm

messages.body_plain:
Hi Victor,
Another example, similar to the one Daniel shared, would be:

gps <- read.csv('gpsfile.csv', header = T)
xy <- cbind(gps$x,gps$y)
a<-project(xy, "+proj=utm +zone=11 ellps=WGS84")  # zone will vary
gps$x<-round(a[,1])
gps$y<-a[,2]
head(gps)

Best,
Esther

messages.body_plain:
Chris,
I got it to work, thanks for the code.
Next question or issue; what can we do if there was no movement? Essentially the same animals at the same site on multiple occasions. From my understanding this will cause us not to estimate sigma, and thus no density? From the secr package I understand you can 'fix' the parameter?
Question is now, in oSCR can we fix sigma to a known length? Second, when  you create the SCRFrame, you can have a look at the mmdm for each session. thus for sessions/sites with no movement data this is NA's. But, let say you have one Session with a mmdm, then this is used as the pooled MMDM? When model fit, will it use the pooled MMDM for each session density?
my model fits, but for the sites with no movement (NA) it gives very high estimates with large CI (e.g. Dens 120 CI 110-1180 per ha), which is nonsense.
Hope this make sense.
Thanks for help

Lourens

messages.body_plain:
Lourens,

If you keep a ‘sigma~1’ model at all times, the sessions with no spatial recaps will ‘borrow’ from the sessions with spatial captures.

Chris
